source.extractedText: Show that the function f : ℕ → ℕ defined by f(x) = 2x − 1 is one-one but not onto.
source.assumption: ℕ = {1,2,3,...}; domain/codomain symbol in PDF text layer corrupt

steps: Take two natural numbers a and b and suppose f(a)=f(b).
Divide both sides by 2: a=b. Different inputs cannot give the same output, so f is one-one.
For each natural number x≥1, f(x)=2x−1 is an odd positive natural number.
The codomain also contains 2, but 2x−1=2 would require x=3/2, which is not a natural number.
Therefore 2 has no preimage. The function is not onto ℕ.
answer: One-one but not onto (assuming positive natural numbers).
